name: Academia Ecuatoriana de la Lengua — Diccionario académico de ecuatorianismos
use: Primary Ecuador lexicon reference. Use to identify regional senses and regional labels; paraphrase entries and write original examples rather than copying definitions or example sentences.

name: Ministerio de Educación — Diccionario académico de ecuatorianismos
use: Searchable entry pages for Ecuadorian words, including guagua, guambra, yapa, yapar, ñañería, and atatay. Use as a source of leads and confirm the current entry before adding it.

name: AEL — Corpus del Habla del Ecuador (CORPHA)
use: Check authentic contexts, region, date, source type, and repeated occurrences. Each app entry should record an actual corpus query before claiming corpus evidence; none of the new entries in this initial update has a logged CORPHA query.

name: ASALE — Diccionario de americanismos
use: Compare country-tagged meanings and register across Spanish varieties. Useful comparisons here include bacán, guagua, atatay, guambra, canguil, and yapa.

name: Carlos Joaquín Córdova — El habla del Ecuador
use: Bibliographic lead for deeper Ecuadorian vocabulary history and usage. Consult the work directly; do not reproduce its entries.

name: Hablemos Ecuatoriano, de chulla vida a YOLO
use: A contemporary reference to explore colloquial phrases. Treat it as a discovery source; create original app explanations and examples.

name: Ecuadorian phraseology study — coastal and Manabí expressions
use: Research lead for fixed expressions and cultural context, with emphasis on the Ecuadorian coast and Manabí. Use the paper as scholarship, not as a pool of text to copy.

name: Ecuadorian Spanish and Quichua contact — phraseology study
use: Research lead on Quichua words in Ecuadorian Spanish phraseological units. Check linguistic and community context before adding etymology or cultural claims.

name: Mitad — Spanish Dictionary for Ecuador
use: The project owner supplied MITAD sunrise and sunset vocabulary and example structures. Use as a cited lead; reuse permissions for its dictionary content are not established.

name: AEL — Fichero de correcciones, precisiones y adendas a la marcación diatópica
use: Use to catch omissions or inaccurate Ecuador geographic labels in broader RAE/ASALE repertories before assigning an Ecuador-specific or regional tag.

name: AEL — Method notes for the Diccionario académico del habla del Ecuador
use: Documents AEL's evidence workflow: CORPHA first, then additional Ecuadorian sources when corpus evidence is insufficient. Use as a model for Habla Ecuador verification.

name: Cuenca air-quality research — Sellers & Espinoza (2017)
use: Two credited Spanish/English abstract sentence pairs power local research-reference retrieval. CC BY 3.0; English is editorially adapted, with subject-expert review pending. Source metadata and license evidence are in data/research-source-manifest.json.

name: Sangay · fish diversity — 2017 research
use: Two credited abstract sentence pairs for local research translation memory. Article-specific CC BY 3.0; English adapted; subject-expert review pending. See data/research-source-manifest.json for provenance.

name: Morona Santiago · bat specimen — 2017 research
use: Two credited abstract sentence pairs for local research translation memory. Article-specific CC BY 3.0; English adapted; subject-expert review pending. See data/research-source-manifest.json for provenance.

name: El Colegio de México — Diccionario del español de México (DEM)
use: Mexican national dictionary. Logged checks now include darle el avión, írsele el avión and echar la hueva; the last retains DEM’s coarse-register label alongside ASALE’s different label.
limits: Only the recorded senses have been inspected. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; no complete dictionary, source definitions or examples imported.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: El Colegio de México — Corpus oral del español de México (COEM)
use: Research route for spoken variation across Mexican regions and cities.
limits: Project description verified; no query or city-specific entry is validated by the project’s existence.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: Academia Mexicana de la Lengua — online reference works
use: Entry point to the academy’s Refranero Mexicano and Diccionario breve de mexicanismos.
limits: Academy catalogue verified; a selected Refranero page returned 403 in the follow-up audit. No proverb was imported from catalogue text or a search snippet.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: Academia Peruana de la Lengua — DiPerú
use: Peruvian national dictionary. Exact sense checks cover floro’s three noun meanings, al toque, a la champa, a la hora de los loros, and aguja with its misio cross-reference.
limits: A headword check does not verify every related locution. DiPerú floro is component-only evidence for meter floro; corpus frequency and local review remain separate.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: Academia Colombiana de la Lengua — Breve diccionario de colombianismos
use: Academy reference for Colombian words and meanings alongside sense-specific ASALE comparisons.
limits: Academy resource page verified. Embedded dictionary access is separate from an individual sense check.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: Instituto Caro y Cuervo — Diccionario de colombianismos
use: Priority regional Colombian reference for vocabulary and expressions.
limits: Official Colombian embassy description verified; dictionary endpoint returned 403 during this audit. No entries were extracted or marked checked against it.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: Fundación Empresas Polar — Diccionario visual del español de Venezuela
use: Publisher-documented, academy-endorsed Venezuelan reference across 14 semantic fields.
limits: Publisher record verified: 268 voices. It is a bounded visual vocabulary, not comprehensive idiom coverage; publication in Caracas is not city usage evidence.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: Carlos Coello Vila / ASALE — Tres estudios sobre el español boliviano
use: Primary regional study of Bolivian Spanish and language contact. The La Paz chapter explicitly documents selected interjections; exact pages are recorded on those entries.
limits: Full scholarly text inspected, including pp. 92–93 of the 2024 reprint. This is not a current frequency survey or a complete imported dictionary. Text is all rights reserved; Habla links and records concise factual meanings with original examples.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: Carlos Coello Vila — El español de Bolivia
use: Primary scholarly discussion of Bolivian vocabulary and regional variation.
limits: The Cervantes page redirected to a maintenance notice on 2026-11-02. Use the separately linked ASALE-hosted Coello book; do not count this page as a completed sense check.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: Elisa García González — Atlas lingüístico de Cuba y Diccionario geolectal
use: Primary author’s study of Cuban geolectal lexicography. It describes locality-linked evidence, phraseological cross-references and the distinction between atlas methodology and dictionary entries.
limits: Full article inspected, especially pp. 195–197. Its atlas fieldwork dates to 1989–1996; the atlas/dictionary application itself remains unaccessed. No present-day frequency, Holguín sense or current city label is inferred.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: RAE / ASALE — CORPES XXI
use: Corroborate phrase use with country, date, genre and spoken/written context; record actual query and concordances.
limits: A corpus link is not a completed query. None of the new phraseology records claims corpus frequency or city validation.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.

name: Instituto Cervantes — Refranero multilingüe
use: Compare proverbial meanings, variants, pragmatic intent, source contexts and English equivalents.
limits: Shared proverb reference; does not establish that a saying is specific to, or common in, any particular country.
importStatus: Reference registered; no complete dictionary or corpus imported.
